fields.meta_title: Legal Workflow Automation for Law Firms | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See legal workflow automation carry one matter through intake, a signed letter, deadline reminders, and pre-bill review. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Legal Workflow Automation for Every New Matter
fields.hero_description: Build legal workflow automation that checks new clients against past matters and holds invoices with the wrong rate.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Law Firm App
fields.features_subheading: Legal workflow automation hands the repeat steps of a matter to software and keeps each judgment call with an attorney.
fields.feature_1:
Describe the firm's process in plain English

Write each rule as a sentence, such as which matter types need a second attorney to approve the letter. Emergent builds the app, its database, and its logic from those sentences.
fields.feature_2:
Connects to the tools the firm runs

The app connects to any tool with an API, so a new matter can sync to your practice management system and a paid invoice to QuickBooks, with data moving in both directions.
fields.feature_3:
Court notices read into the matter record

Upload a court notice, and AI reads the case number and the hearing date into the matter's fields. A field the AI is unsure of goes to a paralegal before the record is saved.
fields.feature_4:
Exceptions reach the attorney who decides

A possible conflict or a rate mismatch goes to one person by Slack, email, or in the app. A reminder follows when nobody acts, then an escalation on the schedule you set.
fields.feature_5:
Matter records in a database the firm owns

Client records and matter records sit in a database you own. Automations run with no task cap, so a busy month with 40 new matters follows the same rules as a month with 4.
fields.feature_6:
Code the firm's IT lead can read

Export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Your IT lead can then review every rule in it before the app touches a single client file or invoice.

fields.tab_content_1:
Quarry Lane Properties shows up on a past matter

Odalys Ferreira-Nakamura's intake for a lease dispute names Quarry Lane Properties LLC as the other party. The app finds that name on past matter M-2291 and holds the engagement letter. Teodora Lindqvist-Amadi, the conflicts attorney, gets a Slack direct message marked Possible conflict, with a Review button.
fields.tab_content_2:
Odalys signs the letter from her phone at 4:12 p.m.

Teodora clears the match, and the app emails Odalys the engagement letter with the $395 hourly rate. She signs it on her phone at 4:12 p.m. The app opens matter M-2318 and assigns it to Bastien Oyelaran-Kroll, the associate who will run the case day to day.
fields.tab_content_3:
November 20 gets three reminders and one escalation

Paralegal Marisol Thackeray-Obuya enters a response date of November 20 on matter M-2318. The app reminds Bastien 14 days before and again 7 days before. On November 18, 2 days before, the draft is still not marked Filed. The app sends a last reminder and emails Rupert Adeyemi-Strand, the supervising partner.
fields.tab_content_4:
The October invoice waits on one $450 entry

The October pre-bill for matter M-2318 comes to $7,847.50: 18.5 hours at $395 make $7,307.50, and one 1.2-hour entry at $450 makes $540.00. Because $450 is not the letter's $395 rate, the app holds the invoice. Ingrid Mbatha-Sorensen, the billing partner, gets a Slack direct message with a Review button.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Legal Workflow Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps that take legal workflow automation from one traced matter to four flows the whole firm runs on new clients.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Trace one closed matter by hand
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write down where each fact lives
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Put each rule in one sentence
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Keep judgment calls with an attorney
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pick a matter that closed last quarter and list each step a person did by hand for it: the intake call, the name search, the letter, the date entry, and the first invoice. Mark the steps that follow a fixed rule, and start with those.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Note which system holds each fact today, such as client names in the practice management system and time entries in the billing tool. Connect each one through its API, and have the app read every fact from the system that owns it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each rule the way you would explain it to a new paralegal: hold the letter when the other party's name appears on a past matter, and remind the associate 14 days before a response date. Paste those sentences into Emergent as the prompt.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which steps the app finishes and which it hands to a person. A name match goes to the conflicts attorney, who decides whether it is a conflict, and a rate mismatch goes to the billing partner. Name one person for each, not a shared inbox.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Run last quarter's intakes and pre-bills through the app before it emails a single client. Compare each flagged name and each held invoice with what people at the firm caught by hand. Fix a rule by prompting, then run the same quarter again.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Turn on pre-bill review first, because no client ever sees it. Read every held invoice for one billing cycle. Add client intake and matter opening next, and leave deadline reminders for last, once every open matter has its dates entered.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once a month, read every item a person had to fix by hand, such as a name match that turned out to be a different company or a rate an attorney changed on purpose. Change the rule behind each repeat with a prompt, and watch whether the list shrinks.

faq_plan.a: Legal workflow automation is the use of technology to streamline, standardize, and automate repetitive legal tasks that lawyers and paralegals previously handled manually. At a firm, that can mean sending deadline reminders or routing a contract through approval, with each step run identically for every client.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up legal workflow automation?
faq_plan.a: Pick one step the firm does the same way on every matter, such as the name search at intake, and describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, which builds it as a working app. Connect your practice management system through its API, test the rule on past matters, and switch it on once the results match.

faq_plan.q: What should legal workflow automation software check before a new matter opens?
faq_plan.a: It should check every name on the intake against past matters and confirm the engagement letter came back signed. Centerbase outlines a new-matter process that runs a conflict check, then sends and receives the engagement letter. An attorney still decides whether a name match is a real conflict.

faq_plan.q: Which steps should law firm workflow automation take on first?
faq_plan.a: Start with the step the firm repeats most often that also follows a fixed rule, such as the name search on every intake. Leave anything that needs an attorney to read the facts out of the first build. Teams outside law pick the same way, and property management automation starts from the steps a landlord repeats for every unit.

faq_plan.q: How does legal workflow automation flag a possible conflict of interest?
faq_plan.a: It matches each name the intake collects, the new client and the other party, against the names on past and open matters, and marks any hit Possible conflict for an attorney to review. Match spelling variants and company suffixes such as LLC as well as exact names. The app only flags the match; the attorney decides what it means.

faq_plan.q: Can legal workflow automation count response deadlines from a date I enter?
faq_plan.a: Yes. It can count days from a date you enter and send reminders at fixed points before it, such as 14 days and 7 days out. Otherwise a paralegal or assistant has to manually calculate relative dates. Have an attorney who knows the court's rules set the rule behind each deadline type and check it before the app relies on it.

faq_plan.q: How should legal workflow automation remind a client to sign the engagement letter?
faq_plan.a: Send a first reminder 2 days after the letter goes out and a second 3 days later, then hand the matter to the attorney to call the client. Stop every reminder the moment the signature comes in. Apps built on Emergent can capture the e-signature and send each reminder by email. Hotel automation runs on the same kind of timer, sending a check-in link 2 days before arrival.

faq_plan.q: How should legal workflow automation limit who sees client files?
faq_plan.a: Give each matter its own access list: the attorneys and staff assigned to it, plus the billing partner for its invoices. Everyone else at the firm sees the matter name but not the files. Emergent builds those roles into the app from a plain-English prompt. Emergent has SOC 2 Type I and ISO 27001.

faq_plan.q: What should legal workflow automation check before invoices go out?
faq_plan.a: Check that every time entry sits on an open matter and has a description of the work, along with the rate check against the engagement letter. Hold any invoice that fails a check for the billing partner instead of sending it. With no task cap on automations built on Emergent, a firm with 300 open matters runs every check each month.

faq_plan.q: Should legal workflow automation follow up with prospects after a consultation?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with a short sequence: one email the day after the consultation with the next step, and a single follow-up a week later. Stop both the moment the prospect signs or says no. Longer email sequences for past contacts belong in a marketing automation workflow, kept apart from the matter records the intake app holds.

This page follows one new matter at a 14-lawyer firm, Brandvold Ilunga LLP, through four flows: an intake form that matches the other party's name against past matters, an engagement letter signed on a phone that opens the matter, reminders before a response date the paralegal entered, and a pre-bill check that holds an invoice when a time entry's rate differs from the letter. The FAQ answers the setup, intake, deadline, document and billing questions a firm operator asks, with sources, and keeps every legal judgment with the attorney.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build Legal Workflow Automation for Every New Matter' and meta title 'Legal Workflow Automation for Law Firms | Emergent' cover the whole matter lifecycle, not invoices alone; hero (116 chars) leads with 'Build legal workflow automation that checks new clients against past matters...'; how-to description is one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Informational, builder-fit SERP: definition in FAQ 1 and the features subheading ('hands the repeat steps of a matter to software and keeps each judgment call with an attorney'), four worked flows on one matter, 7-step how-to, FAQ on conflicts, deadlines, engagement letters, access and pre-bills.

specificity.evidence: Law-firm vocabulary throughout: 'conflicts attorney', 'engagement letter', 'pre-bill', 'response date', 'supervising partner', 'matter M-2318'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Odalys Ferreira-Nakamura's intake for a lease dispute names...', 'Teodora clears the match...', 'Upload a court notice, and AI reads...'.

craft.evidence: No blocking craft defect; long sentences (step 1, 3, 7; FAQ 2, 5) and 'matter' repetition logged as notes.

voice.evidence: Calm, product-led copy with concrete details ('18.5 hours at $395 make $7,307.50', 'signs it on her phone at 4:12 p.m.'); voice notes logged, none blocking.

truth.evidence: Third-party facts sourced: FAQ 1 definition (Spellbook), FAQ 3 'runs a conflict check, then sends and receives the engagement letter' (Centerbase), FAQ 6 'manually calculate relative dates' (Centerbase). Emergent claims map to claims_used (soc2-iso, e-signature-capture, no-caps, alerts, ai-extraction). Numbers check: 18.5x395=7,307.50; 1.2x450=540.00; total 7,847.50. No statements of law or bar duties; legal judgments are left to the attorney ('Have an attorney who knows the court's rules set the rule behind each deadline type').

distinct.evidence: One matter followed through four flows at Brandvold Ilunga LLP; no sibling primary in headings; pre-bill tab is framed as rate check against the engagement letter, not invoice automation.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, no brands or file formats in questions, answer-first; hub link in item 2; sibling links in items 4, 7, 10; secondaries 'legal workflow automation software' (Q3) and 'law firm workflow automation' (Q4).
